summary: Preserve completed mission seat declarations across revision and diagnose missing desired agents

replay.detail: No new full or partial replay trigger. Revision appends canonical intent.desired claims with successor ownership through existing desired selection and replication. Existing stranded generations are not retroactively repaired.

schema.detail: No database tables, indexes, triggers or schema version change. Carry claims add previous owner metadata for incremental invalidation using existing serialized claim bodies.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or digest version change. Both adoption writers recheck carry in their existing transaction and preserve existing revision authority.

compatibility.detail: Completed unchanged steps can retain currently selected stable agent declarations in a successor generation. Unsupported completed declaration carry is refused. Adds operational.failure condition mission-no-eligible-agent with run/generation/step targets and derived currentness by readiness epoch. Existing clients and canonical desired replication remain readable; mixed older reconcilers do not provide the new carry or fault-currentness behavior.

downtime.detail: Executing the fix requires the usual daemon upgrade/restart. Upgrade-to-API and upgrade-to-health interruption have not been measured. Isolated daemon/PTY controls prove unchanged seat processes across mission revision, not production upgrade downtime.

manual.detail: The fix applies to future revisions. A previously stranded run requires an explicit change to its declaring step to execute those declarations again, or a replacement run through normal mission controls. An unchanged completed step does not resurrect an explicit stop or replay one-shot effects. Dynamic names/configuration, completed non-agent effects and reopening after cleanup require an explicit declaring-step change.

recovery.detail: Canonical desired ownership and claim formats remain readable by older builds; no migration must be undone. Returning to an older reconciler restores its prior behavior on later revisions and loses the new derived currentness of missing-agent faults. Eligibility restoration, generation/epoch change and terminal state clear the current fault on the updated reader while immutable operational history remains.
